reviews.text: The hospital is good, but I've been calling for over a week and they never answer. I call every day and nothing happens. It's very annoying.
I went at night and was very well attended to. They are exotic rabbit animals, but our Liry was beyond help 🥺💔 …
5-hour wait

I am waiting for the results of my dog's tests to begin treatment. I haven't received them (they've already been paid for). They don't answer the phone. I've tried three times today, each time for 15 minutes. They also don't respond to emails. I would like to be reimbursed for the 79 euros I paid.

It's ridiculous that none of the veterinary hospital's contact information works after 10 PM.
"We are open for emergencies 24 hours a day, if applicable you can go to the hospital."
How do we know if there is availability to see the animal without contacting them? If it really is an imminent emergency situation?
Do we all rush to the hospital and save yourselves if you can?

I've been calling there for 6 days! To schedule my dog's C-section. 6 days of calling more than 20 times.
It seems like they do it on purpose, so people go to the emergency room and pay more. Improve your customer service!!!

I am leaving this 5-star review as a sincere thank you to the entire team. We arrived at the clinic in a state of great distress regarding our dog. The reception staff's reaction was immediate and exemplary: they stopped everything they were doing upon realizing the animal's condition and immediately took him to the stabilization area. Unfortunately, our companion passed away, but the care he received was impeccable. Furthermore, the humane, warm, and respectful way my wife and I were supported during this difficult time was memorable. We only have positive things to say about this clinic. Thank you for your work and sensitivity.

If it's an emergency, try everyone but this one, because the interest in the dog will be defined by one word: indifference. In a moment of distress and emergency, the disinterest of the team present was so indifferent that it was surprising.
Today was a day to forget, and this university hospital made a big contribution to it.
Thanks for nothing.

Our dog, Snoopy, underwent surgery at the Lusófona University Veterinary Center on July 27, 2026, for an anal hernia.

We were told that the surgery had gone well and that there was no reason to worry.

In the following weeks, Snoopy began to show worrying symptoms: tremors, vomiting, lack of appetite, dark stools, and extreme weakness, to the point of being unable to walk.

After having contacted the veterinarian previously, on August 8th we decided to take him back to the Veterinary Center, as we realized something was wrong.

Snoopy was there for about 6 to 7 hours, during which time he was extremely weak and unable to walk.

After the evaluation, the veterinarian Miguel Martins told us that he couldn't find any problem that justified Snoopy's condition and that the tremors could be related to back pain, so medication was prescribed for that purpose.

However, when we left and requested a copy of the tests to take with us, another colleague from the Veterinary Center, upon checking the results, drew our attention to the fact that Snoopy had a urinary tract infection, information that had not been previously communicated to us.

An antibiotic was then added to the medication.

Days later, Snoopy's condition worsened drastically. He was rushed to the emergency room during the night, with intense tremors and vomiting, and a perforation in his stomach was detected. They tried to operate on him, but his condition was already too critical and Snoopy ended up dying.

We are left with enormous anger and the feeling that the signs presented on August 8th were not properly valued or investigated. We sought help precisely when we realized our dog was very ill and trusted the professionals who were treating him.

We cannot say exactly what the origin of the perforation was, nor can we establish a causal relationship with the surgery without an independent assessment.

However, we believe that the actions and assessment carried out on August 8th raise very serious questions, particularly regarding the tests performed, the interpretation of the results, and the delay in assistance.

This was our experience and, unfortunately, we lost our dog after seeking help and trusting this veterinary service.

We sincerely hope that this situation will be investigated and that other animals and families will not have to go through the same thing.

After several treatments, including an operation that apparently went well! It's completely frustrating to have been trying for 5 consecutive days to contact them to schedule a follow-up appointment, which should have been scheduled for 3 days after the operation, and not get any response or call back. And clearly I'm not going to drive 60km on purpose just to schedule an appointment!
I'm not giving one star because everything else went well!
Improve your customer service/call center.

On the few occasions I went, I actually liked the service. It does take a while, but that's perfectly understandable and normal considering it's a hospital where emergencies sometimes arise and need to be prioritized due to their severity. What I didn't like was how the cordial and friendly service turned into something intimidating because I didn't want to subject my animal to more invasive exams given its debilitated and advanced age. They didn't offer any assistance in trying to help him without invasive exams and told me to bring him back if he gets sick, and to treat the symptoms. I expected more sensitivity and help. But for those who need it, and given today's prices, I think it's worth it; it's always better than not treating at all.
The only veterinarian we trust 😻 …

Highly professional staff, very competent, friendly, and with modern facilities.

I highly recommend them.

Avoid! Terrible service. 1 hour wait just in reception only to be refused admission due to lack of space for hospitalization. And it wasn't for lack of asking beforehand if hospitalization was possible.

On July 7th, we paid the invoice for a consultation that included a blood parasite test. Since then, we have maintained contact via email regarding the payment; however, the results have never been sent to us, and at this point, we no longer receive any response to our messages.

Meanwhile, we were forced to euthanize our dog, so we requested a refund for a service that was never provided. To date, we continue to be completely ignored by the team.

Therefore, I request the immediate refund of €75.15 (Document No.: FT20/3879).

I brought my dog in to see Dr Goncalo Serrano, an internal medicine veterinarian, after she developed chronic vomiting. He was really wonderful with her (and also me, I was quite anxious about her and don’t think I was the easiest patient) and very knowledgeable, and he helped me get her on a hypoallergenic diet, as well as with some initial diagnostics via an ultrasound. It’s a busy hospital so the wait times for further exams can be long, but still, in the meantime she is comfortable and I’m very grateful that she was able to get in here and for Dr Goncalo Serrano’s care and guidance.
I really liked the service; they are very friendly and helpful, and my dog ​​was very well treated.

Terrible. A disgrace. They have one vet available on a Saturday morning for a consultation costing 45 euros. A CT scan costs 235 euros. I waited for 2 hours and still have to wait. A reflection of where we live. A disgrace.

Very attentive, competent, tireless in their pursuit of the best results for our pets, even to the point of research interest, after all, they are a school, understandably! They fail when we need them most, in providing support when there's nothing left to do! Then the abandonment is total! Grateful for the care in any case!
The veterinarians are spectacular, everything is very good, but the reception service is miserable and incompetent, not to mention the phone service, which is very poorly answered.

I thoroughly enjoyed the service. I want to congratulate Dr. Inês Chambel Dias for her professionalism, empathy with pet owners, and care for the animals. I highly recommend her. Thank you very much, Dr. Inês.

I went to this hospital on Saturday, April 18, 2026, with my cat without an appointment because, as I was informed, there are no appointments on weekends! They also told me that because it was the weekend, I would have to wait a little longer, about half an hour! We waited more than two hours to be seen! We ended up giving up and leaving! I'm giving one star because I can't give zero stars! There are many negative reviews, and apparently the hospital isn't at all interested in improving its service! I will never use the services of this establishment again!
If you can, don't come.
We were there today for an emergency appointment and were seen by Dr. Inês, an exemplary doctor! Thank you very much.
They promise good prices for hospitalization and then end up emptying our wallets...

Facilities, medical staff and assistants, no complaints, always ready to help, even the most sensitive.
At the time of registration and when making payments, very slow, very talkative with colleagues, especially Mr. Diogo Jacinto, very distracted, even with a client in front of him, he stops the service to talk to the colleague next to him about how he is going to spend the night.
It's really unbelievable.
Someone asks for information, the answer is "I can't right now".
Since the reception is the "face" of the hospital, shouldn't they have more people attending, more attentive, and informed, in order to be able to answer all existing questions?
I'm sorry...

My dog ​​lost mobility in his hind legs, so I went to this establishment to have an X-ray done. The receptionist, Joana, was very attentive and helped me transport the dog from the car to the building on a stretcher. Dr. Ana, who saw the dog, was also excellent, carefully examining my dog ​​through X-rays, subsequent blood tests, and determining the next steps to take. I highly recommend them.

My dog ​​woke me up in the middle of the night whimpering, and I realized he was in pain because he was having trouble walking. I went to the 24-hour emergency room, but the hospital had no one on the waiting list. Even so, they managed to keep me waiting for almost two hours without any explanation, and with a clearly sick animal. I felt no empathy and ended up leaving without a consultation, going to my usual veterinarian who had already opened. I was very disappointed. Is this the kind of care a veterinary school should provide?
I spent 1 hour and 34 minutes on the phone listening to annoying background music waiting to be answered, and it never happened, so I had to give up.

I was surprised by so many negative reviews. Because my experience couldn't have been better.
The parking is easy to access and free. I had to go to this hospital several times because my cat Leoni was 14 years old and in serious condition, they were always kind and attentive (the whole team), we explained our situation regarding cost containment and they took care to inform us about everything before it was done. Unfortunately, we had to euthanize the cat because he was already suffering a lot, and in such a sad and delicate moment I felt humanity and I can only thank them for doing what they could.
Excellent service. Very good facilities. I recommend it.

As Ki's guardian, a kitten who on October 11, 2025, went to a consultation (and only one!) with Dr. André Meneses at Lusófona University because of a serious mouth infection, and due to what (didn't) happen during her treatment process, I feel the almost obligatory need to inform you that tomorrow marks 15 days since she passed away after a 2-week hospitalization of great struggle and despair.
The only consultation she had with this doctor prescribed some anti-inflammatory tablets and an ointment to put on her gums, Stomodine F, and gave us his contact information so that after a month of treatment we could send him a photo of Ki's mouth so that he could evaluate it and say whether or not a new consultation would be necessary. We did so. A month later we sent the photo of her mouth and waited for his reply. We never received a response. However, her condition worsened again, with constant drooling and severe halitosis to the point where she stopped eating. We had to feed her with a spoon, and it was very painful for her. A month or a month and a half later, we sent her messages again, including a voice message asking for help because she was not doing well at all. Once again, we never received any response from him. We called him several times, and he never answered. Total disinterest.
On December 29th of last year, since she was losing weight and still didn't want to eat and had new symptoms such as urinary incontinence, we went to an emergency consultation at Lusófona University, and we were told that Dr. André Meneses was on vacation.
The infection worsened to such an extent that her kidneys were severely affected, and her creatinine level was 12. They immediately told us that her case was very complicated and that we should expect the worst while believing in the best... she was immediately hospitalized. She had advanced anemia, but an echocardiogram was performed because she was experiencing respiratory difficulties, and a spot was detected on her heart that could indicate pneumonia or a serious infection. She was supposed to receive a blood transfusion, but it was cancelled, as was the IV fluids. She spent a week in intensive care in an oxygen incubator. She showed some improvement, becoming more active, but still refused to eat, so a nasogastric tube was inserted. She then returned to the ward but worsened again and needed oxygen once more. She ended up having total organ failure and passed away two weeks ago, on January 13th.................
We were even asked for a compounded calcium medication, which we promptly had made at a nearby pharmacy, but on the day it was delivered, my dear Ki had passed away..............
We lost our dear and much-loved Ki. I know nothing will bring her back, but I wanted to express my total disillusionment and disappointment with this reputable doctor for having been "forgotten." The medical team that assisted her was impeccable and tireless, and despite some reservations, they ended up confirming that if Ki had been assisted from the beginning, she could still be alive.
Our biggest mistake was trusting and believing the words of a doctor who never called back to Ki's situation, and we should never have expected him to contact us as agreed, never. That guilt will die with me; I will never forgive myself.
My criticism is not directed at FMV Universidade Lusófona, about whom I have nothing to say, but specifically at this doctor, Dr. André Meneses, to whom I should never have entrusted my beloved cat.

The Lusófona Veterinary Hospital has good facilities and a very attentive team, especially in their treatment of animals. I went with my dog ​​without an appointment and, although the wait was long (I arrived around 6/7 pm and left around 11 pm), I consider it understandable, since she was seen for a consultation and had tests done.
The consultation fee was €21.50, which I consider adequate. Regarding contact, I do not recommend the telephone, as it is very difficult to get through to calls; however, contact by email usually works quite well.
On a less positive note, the coffee machine only accepts coins, not allowing cards or MB Way, which ends up being a bit inconvenient during long waiting periods.
Overall, I was satisfied with the service and the care shown to my dog.

Easy to locate and park. The facilities are always very clean.
It's understandable that without a scheduled appointment, you might wait longer than you'd like, and if an emergency comes in, it's even worse, delaying everything. And being a university veterinary hospital, it's even more natural that the team is rarely the same; they have rotating schedules, and the team is smaller on weekends.
But from the telephone service to the in-person service, they were always helpful.
Most importantly, the service from the entire team was always very professional, the facilities were always clean, and the conditions of the kennels are impeccable, in terms of comfort and hygiene.
On the day of admission, they were attentive, and the information provided was simple and clear.
We thank everyone, especially on the last day... from the service of the assistant and the doctor on duty with whom we spoke, to the way they received us, empathetic, caring, and very understanding of the circumstances.
Communication was always simple, clear, and enlightening regarding the necessary information about the situation in question.
Thank you very much to the whole team.
They never answer the phone. Unbelievable for a university.

I would like to thank the team at the Lusófona University Veterinary Hospital. My Yoda, who was very dear and spoiled, was cared for with affection, professionalism, and sensitivity. Dr. A.R.S. was especially dedicated and attentive. We felt that he was safe and well cared for until the very last moment. I wholeheartedly recommend this hospital to everyone who wants the best for their animals.
A big thank you to all the professionals at this hospital.
Excellent clinical care, both in technical and scientific terms, as well as in relational terms!

We arrived at 5:50 PM, it's now 9:21 PM and we're still waiting for someone to tell us about the cat's results. I've already asked twice and the answer is always the same: "The doctors are in an emergency room right now," but everyone who arrived later has already been seen and gone on with their lives. I don't recommend them and I hope I don't have to come back.

This hospital is in total disrepair. I can't understand how this service serves as a school to train veterinarians. A miserable service from scheduling to hospitalizations. My cat has been hospitalized since Monday. They say they'll call to inform me about her condition, but they don't. I call dozens of times, waiting 40 minutes on each call until I give up because no one answers.
My cat needed urgent surgery, they asked me to wait and that they would call during the following week to schedule the operation. Three weeks passed, and only then did they operate on my cat. At the first consultation, they told us about a complex operation involving the complete removal of the inner ear, but they didn't give us any reason to worry; on the contrary, they said it was the only way for her to improve and live longer with a good quality of life. The day of the operation arrives, and they call to tell us to get ready because they removed her ear. Since Monday, the cat hasn't eaten; I had to go to the hospital to deliver liquid pâtés. When I arrived, I realized that in addition to my cat now having no ear, she also had a paralyzed eye. I called to find out how she spent the night, but no one answered. This hospital should be closed. The people who work there, however nice they may be, are not well-equipped, and often end up dealing with the frustration of clients due to this chaos on the part of the management. I have entered this hospital many times and there were clients complaining about situations similar to mine.
They removed my cat's ear, and I don't know what happened during the operation, but in addition to having no ear, my cat ended up losing her sight as well. It is unacceptable; in the consultation before the operation, we asked 20 times if the operation was really necessary because we never wanted to see Mel suffer. Mel is 12 years old, and we always preferred that she have a peaceful end of life instead of wasting away alone in a place where (I'd bet my life on it) she is not given the proper attention or treated with the affection she deserves.
Please, for your sake and for the sake of your pets, do not use this veterinarian.

Complete lack of control from the staff. They left my kitten to feed herself with a tube alone, and the result was death from asphyxiation pneumonia. I will never go to this hospital again; they play with lives! May karma catch up with you.

From the reception staff to the medical team, I have nothing but good things to say. Helpful, approachable, and good professionals. The facilities aren't luxurious, but compared to other hospitals/clinics, the prices are more affordable.
Even after reading the comments, I still decided to try to schedule a specialist appointment I was referred to… 40 minutes on hold and nothing 😓 …

Phones are never answered, emails take weeks to get a reply. They schedule appointments, then reschedule them between appointments without informing the client. In short, I don't recommend them at all, because if the doctors' time is important, ours is just as valuable.

In the space of a year, I had two experiences visiting this hospital, both of them in serious situations involving visits to the emergency room, surgery, hospitalization, and finally, going through a euthanasia procedure.

I agree that it is difficult to contact the hospital's services by phone, but the last time I went, I noticed that they were trying to improve this service.

My experiences, apart from actually having to wait some time in an emergency setting, were very good! Being a university veterinary hospital, it is more difficult to provide care during school holidays.

I highlight and emphasize the professionalism, care, empathy, and dedication of all the professionals I encountered (doctors, nurses, assistants, and receptionists), especially during such a difficult and painful time! I had two children with me, and it was noticeable how much care they gave us, giving us time and space, welcoming us with affection and empathy during this difficult time! I can't find beautiful words to express how well they supported us and how I felt during this very important moment for us!

A simple thank you will certainly not be enough to express this gratitude!
Rude. Lack of empathy right from the start.

I don't understand what's been going on with the hospital lately. On Saturday, I had an emergency and waited for 6 hours, while there were people with emergencies who had been waiting for 8 hours. The hospital is having serious staff reduction problems that need to be resolved.

The hospital is often abandoned with no one at reception, they don't answer any of the available phone numbers, and they don't respond to emails.

On Sunday (the following day), I had another emergency episode. I entered the hospital and there was no one there, not even one person at the counter, nothing. I had to take my cat into the restricted area to get treatment. After what happened to me, a woman entered the hospital with a small dog in her arms, breathing extremely heavily, for the emergency. She also didn't know what to do because there was no one there. I had to guide the woman to the restricted area and look for someone inside the hospital, as I did.

I admitted my cat to the hospital yesterday at 3 PM, with the promise that I would receive an update on her condition that same day. I called the hospital at 6 PM and was told that the doctor was attending to an emergency and would call me back later to discuss my cat's condition.

At 8 PM I called again because no one had contacted me. They said the doctor couldn't talk because he was in consultation and that he would definitely call me this morning to discuss my cat's condition.

Today it's 3 PM, the doctor hasn't called me, they're not answering my calls, and I can't get any information about my hospitalized cat.

On January 20th, 2025, an urgent appointment, waiting time approximately 3 hours, considering your information (I don't remember the receptionist's name) that there were no people ahead of us. Today, January 27th, 2025, the same situation occurred; they informed us (Rafael) that the service would be quick, but more than 3 hours have already passed. Lack of organization, and possibly a lack of staff. Shameful... edit to the criticism: at 10:03 PM we were finally seen, thanks to some people who had been waiting for a discharge for 1 hour and 30 minutes, who started knocking on all available doors (there was no one left at reception). A staff member appeared, and we took the opportunity to explain our situation as well. They were not informed that there were more people in the waiting room; they only registered us in the system at 9 PM (information provided). As an aside, on this day, January 27, 2025, we paid close attention to potentially "more urgent" situations, which was not the case here. Excellent work, Rafael! Thanks to your competence and professionalism, we were able to be assisted quickly. Please provide training to the person in question and the other reception staff so that these situations do not occur.
They don't answer the phone no matter what.
Absolutely miserable experience, endless waiting, zero communication, rude staff, no space in the waiting room, and utter disorganization and amateurism. DO NOT TRUST YOUR ANIMALS TO THESE PEOPLE!

Terrible experience I had today, it was the first and last time.

I traveled all the way from Seixal specifically to have an appointment with Dr. Rui Onça, an appointment scheduled more than a month ago, for 4 PM today.
Unfortunately, coming from Seixal, I encountered some traffic and only managed to arrive at 4:30 PM, where I took a number and was only seen at 5 PM.
I was immediately denied the appointment by Dr. Rui Onça.

I just want to thank the receptionist who, even being completely alone, did his best in attending to all the clients and the overload of tasks he had on him, even after explaining this on the phone, the doctor didn't want to know.

I just have this to say about Dr. Rui Onça's terrible attitude, it's recorded and crossed off my list.

And put more professionals at reception!
I hope my dog's problem gets resolved today, or tomorrow in principle. Today I've been waiting almost a month for medication for my dog, Oscar.
Great professionals, everything was excellent.

It's a University Hospital, it has cheaper services than other vets, which is why more people end up wanting to use its services.
They were super helpful and attentive, the waiting time for the walk-in emergency was 3 hours, which was to be expected considering it was late afternoon on a weekday.

Terrible service during visits. There's a 2 or 3 hour visiting period, but they only start calling visitors at the end of that time, and it's one visit per day per animal. The delay is incomprehensible.
They don't answer the phones... I've been calling for 4 days and nothing.
Very bad!! Lack of professionalism, merchants!! To be avoided.
